rationale: Pulp's Development Inspector consumes a gpu_submission_observed frame flag that no production host ever set, so the standalone startup trial could never claim submission evidence even on a healthy GPU frame. WindowHost therefore gains two conservative append-only queries at the public vtable tail: whether the host can answer for submission at all, and whether the last rendered frame reached its intended output. The macOS GPU host is the only implementer; it records the existing render::frame_reached_output() verdict that already governs damage retirement, so a recreate outcome reports false and an absent producer keeps the false default. The standalone inspector's frame-evidence producer reads that query for the frame it just captured. Hosts on every other platform are unchanged. This is Pulp-specific developer-tool and standalone-host observability wiring with no counterpart framework behavior to backport.
